claim: Introducing [59] I’ll go with them, if only to get some exercise: “There is a use of if only distinct from that considered in §14.1.3 above”.
evidence_summary: §14.1.3 (p. 746, “If in combination with only and even”) treats only if and even if, and doesn’t discuss the sequence if only. The wish use is in §14.2.1, p. 751, under the heading If only: “Quite distinct from only if is the construction where only occurs in the protasis indicating something like a wish”. Ch. 10, p. 945 cites “see Ch. 8, §14.2.1” for if only with a modal preterite.
finding: Medium confidence. Change §14.1.3 to §14.2.1. The defence that §14.1.3 is where an if phrase is the scopal focus of only (p. 746) fits the contrast in focus, but p. 757 contrasts two uses of the sequence if only, and p. 751 introduces that sequence.
proposed_wording: There is a use of if only distinct from that considered in §14.2.1 above
inference: Which section treats the if only that p. 757 sets its new use against?

evidence.passage: §14.4, p. 757. “There is a use of if only distinct from that considered in §14.1.3 above”
evidence.example: Page 751, heading If only. Ch. 10, p. 945, “see Ch. 8, §14.2.1”.
evidence.establishes: The wish use of if only is in §14.2.1.
